title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 15
statement: Recall that the conjugate of the complex number \(w = a + bi,\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers and \(i = \sqrt{-1},\) is the complex number \(\overline{w} = a - bi.\) For any complex number \(z,\) let \(f(z) = 4i\overline{z}.\) The polynomial \[ P(z) = z^4 + 4z^3 + 3z^2 + 2z + 1 \] has four complex roots: \(z_1,\) \(z_2,\) \(z_3,\) and \(z_4.\) Let \[ \begin{aligned} &Q(z) = z^4 + Az^3 + Bz^2 \\ &\quad {}+ Cz + D \end{aligned} \] be the polynomial whose roots are \(f(z_1),\) \(f(z_2),\) \(f(z_3),\) and \(f(z_4),\) where the coefficients \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) and \(D\) are complex numbers. What is \(B + D?\)

solutions.text:
By Vieta on \(P,\) \(\sum_{i\lt j} z_iz_j = 3\) and \(\prod z_j = 1,\) both real, so their conjugates are also \(3\) and \(1.\)

The roots of \(Q\) are \(4i\overline{z_j}.\) Then \(B\) is the sum of products of pairs: \(B = (4i)^2 \sum_{i\lt j}\overline{z_i}\,\overline{z_j}\) \(= -16 \cdot 3 = -48.\) And \(D = (4i)^4 \prod \overline{z_j} = 256 \cdot 1 = 256.\)

So \(B + D = -48 + 256 = 208.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The elementary symmetric functions of \(\overline{z_j}\) are the conjugates of those of \(z_j;\) all of \(P\)’s coefficients are real, so those symmetric sums are real
